title: "Without doing" in Japanese: 〜ずに | Learn Japanese with The Spider's Thread (Akutagawa)
hook: How do you say "without doing" in Japanese?
body: 小《ちい》さな蜘蛛《くも》を、踏《ふ》まずに助《たす》けたのです。
translations: He spared a little spider instead of stepping on it.

breakdown.ja: 小《ちい》さな蜘蛛《くも》を
breakdown.note: ちいさな = small (used only before a noun). を marks the object.
〜ずに = "without ~ing" (like 〜ないで). ふむ → ふま + ずに
〜のです explains: "(you see,) he saved it."

source: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa, "The Spider's Thread" (1918), Aozora Bunko — retold in simple Japanese
